event.details: Aṅga, a descendant in Dhruva’s line, righteously protects people like father. His wife is Mṛtyu’s UNNAMED daughter; their son Vena is cruel. Exhausted by failed instruction, Aṅga abandons kingdom and goes forest sorrowfully. Robbers plunder rulerless land; frightened people seek Brahmins, who enthrone Vena in paternal realm. He kills robbers but abandons proper conduct, hurting varṇa/āśrama practitioners. Sages restrain him; he claims everyone should worship him as protector. Angry Brahmins kill him by curse.

event.details: Sages churn Vena’s LEFT aṅga/body-part seeking king; cruel sin-formed man arises, short, dusky, bearded and tawny-eyed. They say niṣīda; he becomes named Niṣāda, receives forest station and Niṣādas descend from him. They then churn RIGHT aṅga; an energetic COUPLE emerges, both Viṣṇu-kalā-associated. Couple bows to Brahmins; male is consecrated king and named Pṛthu, upholding royal dharma/prosperity. Neither left thigh/right arm specificity nor partner name Arci is supplied.

event.details: After time people lack food and seek Pṛthu. Earth swallowed resources under Vena’s adharma and cannot return them under righteous king. Angry Pṛthu draws bow/arrow to kill Earth; she flees in cow form and he pursues like Yama. Finding no refuge, she seeks Pṛthu with folded hands, asks him not to kill woman/cow/Earth and protect surrendered one. He threatens death unless she manifests varied food always. Earth says plants already consumed cannot be directly returned; asks first leveling, then calf and milker so cow-form yields all plants as milk. Killing would be futile without these arrangements.

event.details: Pṛthu crushes mountains with bow-tip, levels Earth and arranges towns/villages; source says this starts their arrangement. He makes Earth his DAUGHTER by adoption/putrītva, so she is called Pṛthvī. With Manu as CALF, Pṛthu himself MILKS six-taste food-milk. Beings of three worlds then obtain their own food-milk. Adoption and calf-role are not biological parentage.

event.details: Milking roles: Veda-form Brahmā CALF/Bṛhaspati MILKER takes milk; 36 does not separately name its substance. Rudra CALF/Kālāgnirudra MILKER yields flesh-form Hara-life milk. Viṣṇu CALF/Yajamāna MILKER yields act-born sacrifice-support milk. Sun CALF/Dhruva MILKER yields luminaries’ life. Śeṣa CALF/Vāsuki MILKER yields serpent food. Śiva CALF/Nandikeśvara MILKER yields knowledge/vidyā milk. These are source-specific cosmic milking roles, not parents/children; Rudra and Śiva labels retained separately in this table.

event.details: Mobile/immobile beings and lords milk Pṛthu-prepared Earth. He honors and joyfully protects her as daughter; she remains happy. He rules Earth as emperor and undertakes hundred horse sacrifices with great dakṣiṇā. Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śaṅkara, Indra-led gods, Gandharvas, Kaśyapa-led sages, Śeṣa-led Nāgas and varied people with wives come. Hundred opening count is kept distinct from final NINETY-NINE completion at 52.

event.details: As last sacrifice begins, worried Indra in matted hair/rags steals horse. Pṛthu’s UNNAMED son sees him but lets him go as ascetic; Indra leaves horse and disappears afraid. Next he uses bone-bearing/ash-smeared disguise and son does not strike him. Altogether Indra steals horse SIX TIMES. Pṛthu prepares to kill him; Brahmā consoles/restrains him, and Indra is not killed. Pṛthu completes NINETY-NINE sacrifices. Urged by Brahmā, Indra bows; Pṛthu renounces enmity and embraces him. Honored gods/guests depart; Pṛthu resumes righteous protection.
event.outcome: 99 sacrifices; Indra survives, bows and is embraced; Pṛthu resumes rule.
